record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: Is the jump operation on Weihrauch degrees definable from the remaining structure and operators already under discussion?

evidence.quote: Another line of questions concerns definability of operators from others. As supremum and infimum, we know ⊔ and ⊓ to be definable in terms of ≤W. It is easy to see that ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W and ×, in very much the same way that Westrick’s result has shown ⋄ to be definable from 1, ≤W and ⋆. By definition, → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W. What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure? What about the jump of Weihrauch degrees (cf. [6])?

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Andrews–Lempp–Marcone–Miller–Valenti, arXiv:2402.13163, 2024/2025) introduces and studies a "totalizing" jump operator on Weihrauch degrees and analyzes its algebraic properties, but does not appear to settle whether the standard parallelization jump is first-order definable from the rest of the Weihrauch structure. No source found that explicitly resolves the definability question.

status_evidence.title: A jump operator on the Weihrauch degrees
status_evidence.snippet: We provide an explicit definition for an operator on partial multi-valued functions that, when lifted to the Weihrauch degrees, induces a jump operator (the totalizing jump).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies a jump operator on Weihrauch degrees but does not settle the definability of the parallelization jump from the remaining structure.

status_evidence.title: Weihrauch Complexity in Computable Analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Weihrauch complexity discussing operators on Weihrauch degrees including the jump.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys treat the jump as a primitive operator without giving a definability reduction to ≤_W and the algebraic operators.
